5. ECS tone in IBD

There is disagreement on the tone of the ECS between studies of human IBD [summarised in Figure 1]. CB1 has been identified in the colonic epithelium [particularly cryptiồạ, some plasma cells of the lamna propria, smuoth muscle, and the submucosal myenteric plexusạConversely, CB2 localises in the absorptive and goblet cells of the epithelium, Paneth cells, and some subepithelial macrophages and plasma cells, "19 CB2 was expressed at slightly higher levels than CB1 in one study. The effect of inflammation on expression of CB1 and CB2 is less clear. Increases in both CB1 and 2 in both CD and

'acute phase IRD' [a combination of UC and IRD-unclassified]i have been observed. The authors of this study suggest that the changes in CB1 may be an effect of goblet cell depletion in epithelial architec ture rather than a true increase in protein abundance. In other work, increases in either CB15 or alternatively in CB2 alone have been observed. A recent study of CB1 and CB2 gene expression in Crohn's disease, the largest to date, demonstrated consistent detection of expression albeit at low levels in inflamed, non-inflamed, and healthy samples. A difference in expression patterns was seen between disease affecting the ileum, where both CB1 and 2 were reduced in inflamed! non-inflamed samples, and colon, where an increase was seen in CB1 and 2 in the non-inflamed but not inflamed samplesại

Similar controversy exists for levels of endocannabinoids themselves. AFA has been shown to be increased in inflamed samples from UC patients, "98 yet reduced in another study." It is more plausible that AEA levels are indeed decreased in inflammation as it has been shown that there is reduced expression of the synthetic enzyme NAPE-PID and increased expression of the hydrolytic enzyme FAAH in colonic inflammationiAse PEA is increased in inflammation in one study but does not change in another;" and the two studies assessing 2AG levels both demonstrate no change in inflammation. 45

To date, only one study has attempted to define levels of MGLI. and the DAGL enzymes in human IBDạiMGLL was localised to the central portion of epithelial cells, polymorphonuclear cells of the lamina propria, and the myenteric plexus, and was shown to be increased in inflammation. Previously MGIL. has been shown to be widely distributed in the rat intestine, increasing in expression from duodenum to distal coloniại DAGLe was similarly increased in inflammation, but no difference was seen in DAGLß.

There are a multitude of potential explanations for the differences hetween these studies. In particular, the patients studied were not always well phenotyped for disease severity and extent, and were trequently grouped together. Furthermore, the potential role of medications such as systemic immunosuppression in altering expression levels was not explored. In many studies, comparisons were made between inflamed mucosa in an IBD patient and healthy mucosa from a different person. ECS tone has been shown to be affected by diurnal variation and ethniciry not to mention the likely confounder of any comorbidities such as irritable bowel syndrome, in which the involvement of the ECS is well documented." Definitive annotation of ECS component distribution in the intestine will benefit from development of more sensitive and specific antibodies.

Interestingly, CBD reduces iNOS and S100B expression in cultured colonic biopsies from patients with UC, indicating effects on enteric glial cell activation.
